title: Generosity part 1
devotional:
Have you ever felt lost in a crowd, maybe it has been at some sporting event, or a concert or even in a large city where there is hundreds or even thousands of people? There is lots of noise, activity, hustle and bustle. And you feel unnoticed, passed by, a total stranger among so many people, you blend in so much that you become invisible. Many people live their whole lives like that. Mr. and Mrs. anonymous, nameless faces in the sea of humanity, unseen by the vast majority. Many find the crowd the loneliest place on earth; others believe that in the whole scheme of things their life isn’t that important any way. They think ‘my life will make no difference,’ they believe that mediocrity is normal. So they accept the lie that says ‘stay lost in the crowd.’ They believe the lie that says ‘the life you are living is of very little if any consequence if any. You don’t matter, you don’t count!’ So they spend their whole life lost in the crowd.

I want us to meet someone who stood out from the crowd. The interesting thing is that we virtually know nothing about him. We don’t know his name, we don’t know anything about his family, we know nothing about his education or if he had any special gifts. What we do know about him does not really help us.

He was a boy, The word John uses for you boy is paidarrion. The only other time this word is found in the New Testament is Matthew 11:16. This word is often used in critical literature to describe a child slave. We have no way of knowing if this young boy was a slave. If he was I think it brings a new dimension to this story

He was poor. {we know he was poor because only poor people ate barley bread.}

So if you were trying to describe him what we know about him doesn’t really help. Yet he stood out from the crowd, he made a difference, his life touched thousands, history would remember him. He is an example to millions. When we read about him in the Bible, we read just 12 words. Imagine having a 12 word biography!

“Here is a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish.” His biography was as small as his lunch. But he stood out from the crowd. Why? because he was generous.

This young boy has a lot to teach us about generosity.

Generosity means that we respond appropriately to the circumstances around us. There may have been up to 10,000 people there on that day. We are told there were 5000 men; there must have been women and children. The people had been with Jesus for three days and they were hungry, and had no food. So this young boy gives to Jesus all the food he has.

I don’t think this young boy had any idea what Jesus was going to do; I don’t think he said to himself ‘I am going to make sure that all these people get fed.’ Nor did he try and rationalize away his opportunity to respond to this humanitarian crisis. He did not say ‘All I have is five barley and two small fish, what difference will that make?’ The amazing thing is how Jesus receives these bread and fish. John writes in 6:11 ‘’Jesus then took the loaves, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted. He did the same with the fish.’’

Jesus was thankful for the little this young boy had to give him. I can understand why we should be thankful to Jesus for what he gives to us. But, Jesus being thankful for the very little we give to him, that is amazing.

Think of the circumstances of your life, the place where you live, the people that surround you, how do you think a generous person would respond in that situation?

Generosity will allow us to engage with the heart of Jesus. In giving his bread and fish this boy was sharing something of the heart of Jesus, he was looking at others in the same way Jesus was. The disciples saw the crowds as a problem. They said, ‘Send the crowds away so they can go to the villages and buy themselves food.’ In other words, ‘They’re not our problem!’ The young boy’s attitude was so different, ‘Lord I don’t have much, but the little I do have you can have it all.’ Generosity requires that we have ‘A Christ like,’ world-view.

What difference would it make if we saw the world in which we lived through the eyes of Jesus?

Generosity will help us discover our full potential.

When we begin to live lives that are distinguished by generosity, that will bring the best out of us, which will make our lives more significant.

Generosity will affect how you view and manage your resources. Sometimes we try to justify or rationalise our lack of generosity. We think that we need to have more before we can be generous. But generosity has nothing to do with how much we have, or how little, it is about the condition of our hearts, affecting how we view our possessions and resources. You can have a lot and be mean and tight fisted. You can also be poor with little and be a very generous person. If we are not generous with the little we have, then we won’t be generous if we have a lot.

We all find it so easy to hold on to what we have got. Can you think of some generous act you would like to do for someone this week?

Generosity is something God loves to bless.

There is a line in the story that is often overlooked. ‘Jesus then took the loaves, gave thanks and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted. He did the same with the fish.’ Why was Jesus so thankful for this meagre gift of food? There was nothing special about this bread and fish. However, this bread and fish gave Jesus an opportunity to share his heart of love and compassion for those who were around him, which was why he was so thankful. Any opportunity that Jesus has to use our expressions of generosity to bless others, will cause him to be thankful.
prayer: Father thank you I am in the right place to be generous and I have all I need to be generous.
